newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends down after range-bound session.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends down after range-bound session.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed about $2 weaker on Thursday, after hovering in a tight $172-$174 a tonne holding pattern, with brokers reporting thin volumes and a market dancing mainly to the tune of NYMEX heating oil.
"What the market really needs is some headline driven trading to break us out of this range," said one trader.
April gas oil reached a high of $174.25 before slipping to a close of $173.25, $2.00 down on the day, but $1.25 above the day's low.
The inactivity in the April market had some traders reshifting their principle focus to May.
Progress on Friday above Thursday's $174.50 a tonne close could herald further gains, brokers said.
"Our May continuation charts indicate any movement above this level tomorrow morning will be the screen's key indicator," another trader said.
IPE Brent appeared to be taking some heart from news that two European refiners were restoring throughputs to normal levels, following the weak-margin related runcuts seen over the past two weeks.
By 1806 GMT, May Brent was trading seven cents firmer at $20.39 a barrel, just six cents off the session high.
A bounce off technical support in the $20.07 a barrel area was also helping Brent, dealers said.
Traders said crude runs at Texaco Netherlands' 400,000 bpd Rotterdam refinery, a 35-65 joint venture with British Petroleum, were returning to normal.
